Identified as this feast because: Commons' description, from the Walters Art Museum's own catalogue, says the icon was displayed in a church on the feast day of Christ's Transfiguration, 6 August - the day this record keeps. Commons describes it: An icon such as this would have been displayed in a church on the feast day of Christ's Transfiguration (August 6) to be venerated by the faithful. The abrasion of Christ's image on it bears witness to such veneration by touch and kiss. Because of its small size, the image may have also been used privately, possibly by a monk.
